title: How long to boil an egg for soft, medium, and hard
summary: Approximate hot-start timings: 6 minutes soft, 8 medium, 11–12 hard; use a separate timer.

blocks.title: Choose a time, then start your timer
blocks.body: Lower large fridge-cold eggs gently into already-boiling water; start timing as they enter and maintain a gentle boil. Start around 6 minutes for soft, 8 for medium, or 11–12 for hard. Egg size, starting temperature and altitude change the result; cool promptly when done.

blocks.heading: Approximate timing guide · no countdown runs here

items.title: Soft
items.detail: Target: set white and runny yolk; results vary.

items.title: Medium
items.detail: Yolk goes jammy at the edges and stays soft in the middle. The egg-salad and ramen sweet spot.

items.title: Hard
items.detail: Target: set yolk. Check the result and adjust the next batch; doneness is not guaranteed by the clock.

blocks.title: When the count ends
blocks.body: Use a separate kitchen or phone timer. This timeline has no start button or alarm. Transfer eggs carefully to ice water when the timer finishes.

items.label: Hot-start boiling method
items.detail: Method and approximate soft/medium/hard timing; both comparison pages use the same assumptions.
